title: System Calls and the Userspace Boundary

content.intro: This lesson introduces system calls and the userspace boundary as part of linux kernel, hardware, and system internals. Begin with an observation you can safely repeat, then explain what the result tells you and what it does not prove.
content.why_it_matters: Relate kernel interfaces, processes, memory, modules, drivers, and hardware discovery to observable system behavior.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Linux exposes kernel and hardware state through documented interfaces such as procfs, sysfs, system calls, and device management tools.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: First, state what you expect from the example. Run it in the intended environment, capture standard output and any error message, and inspect the exit status where meaningful. Then connect the observation to this lesson: System Calls and the Userspace Boundary. Do not infer more than the evidence supports.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake
content_blocks.text: A common mistake is to assume system calls and the userspace boundary behaves identically on every distribution, kernel, utility version, and administrative policy. Verify the installed tool and consult the matching manual before using the procedure elsewhere.

content_blocks.title: Safety and compatibility
content_blocks.text: PIDs and formatting vary. Inspect your own process and do not signal unrelated processes. For commands that edit files, manage services, change network/firewall state, partition disks, change permissions recursively, or alter boot settings, use an isolated VM, take a snapshot/backup, review the exact target, and prepare a recovery path before acting.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the command is missing, check whether the required package is installed and which distribution you are using. If access is denied, do not immediately escalate to root; confirm the target path, identity, and required permission. If the result differs, capture the command, output, version, and environment so the issue can be reproduced.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: Remember the core relationship: Linux exposes kernel and hardware state through documented interfaces such as procfs, sysfs, system calls, and device management tools. The goal is to explain the observed result, test a boundary case, and record a limitation rather than memorize a command in isolation.

content.task: In an isolated Linux lab, investigate system calls and the userspace boundary. Use the guided example as a starting point, record the output/status, and test one boundary, failure, or distribution-specific case. Explain what you learned without changing a production system.
